title: Redirection
subtitle: fds, operators, pipes, here docs, special files

cards.meaning: The three default open files — keyboard, screen, error messages to the screen
cards.notes: Redirection = capture output from a file/command/script and send it as input elsewhere.

cards.meaning: File descriptors for stdin, stdout, stderr
cards.notes: Every open file gets a file descriptor.

cards.meaning: Extra file descriptors for temporary duplicate links
cards.notes: Assign one to stdin/stdout/stderr as a spare copy so you can restore 0/1/2 after complex redirection.

cards.meaning: Open filename for reading on stdin (fd 0)
cards.notes: Same idea as cat filename | grep search-word. Use n< for fd n.

cards.meaning: Open filename for writing on stdout (fd 1) — create or truncate
cards.notes: Missing file → create. Existing file → wipe to zero size. Use n> for fd n.

cards.meaning: Truncate file to zero length via the null command
cards.notes: : is the null command (special characters). Opens for write and truncates.

cards.meaning: Same truncate as : > filename, but not in every shell
cards.notes: Works in Bash; other shells may reject bare > filename.

cards.meaning: Open filename for appending on stdout (fd 1); create if missing
cards.example: echo one > file; echo two >> file
cards.notes: > replace. >> add to the end. Use n>> for fd n.

cards.meaning: Redirect both stdout (1) and stderr (2) to filename — preferred form
cards.notes: Semantically equivalent to >filename 2>&1.

cards.meaning: Other form of redirecting stdout and stderr together
cards.notes: Of the two forms, &>filename is preferred.

cards.meaning: Send fd 2 to wherever fd 1 currently goes
cards.notes: Makes &>filename / >filename 2>&1 equivalent for capturing both streams.

cards.meaning: > redirects stdout only — stderr still hits the screen
cards.example: java -version > version  → banner on screen, version empty
cards.notes: java -version writes its banner on stderr.

cards.meaning: Redirect stderr only
cards.notes: Captures errors (here, the whole java -version banner) into the file.

cards.meaning: Suppress all of a command’s output
cards.notes: Throw everything away.

cards.meaning: Pipe — stdout of one process becomes stdin of the next
cards.notes: Similar to > but chains processes. | = next command’s stdin; > = a file.

cards.meaning: Array of exit codes for each command in a pipe
cards.notes: Three commands → three statuses. Stored in $PIPESTATUS.

cards.meaning: Append to a file and still print to stdout
cards.notes: Screen and append to file.

cards.meaning: Here document — stdin is the lines until a line containing only the delimiter
cards.notes: Closer is only the delimiter, no trailing blanks. That delimiter line is not stored in the output.

cards.meaning: Here string — expanded word fed as stdin (stripped-down here document)
cards.notes: Instead of echo "$VAR" | grep -q txt. No pipe, no echo.

cards.meaning: If fd is a valid integer, file descriptor fd is duplicated
cards.notes: Bash handles this filename specially in redirections.

cards.meaning: File descriptor 0 is duplicated
cards.notes: Special filename for stdin.

cards.meaning: File descriptor 1 is duplicated
cards.notes: Special filename for stdout.

cards.meaning: File descriptor 2 is duplicated
cards.notes: Special filename for stderr.

cards.meaning: Open a TCP connection to host:port (Bash special filename)
cards.notes: host = hostname or Internet address; port = integer or service name.

cards.meaning: Open a UDP connection to host:port (Bash special filename)
cards.notes: Same host/port rules as /dev/tcp/…

cards.meaning: Open file for read and write on file descriptor n
cards.notes: n<> = read+write on fd n (spare descriptor 3–9).

cards.meaning: Write to file descriptor n
cards.notes: Sends the GET request to fd 5 in the TCP example.

cards.meaning: Read from file descriptor n
cards.notes: Reads the response from fd 5 in the TCP example.

cards.meaning: Redirect a whole code block / loop so its stdin is file
cards.example: while [ ... ]; do read name; echo $name; let "count += 1"; done < file
cards.notes: Each read takes the next line. Same idea as cat file | … but applied to the loop.
